data.hook: Patrick Mahomes returns from ACL surgery, but an undrafted rookie steps in to protect his blind side against Denver's fierce pass rush.
data.name: Chiefs Rule Out Simmons and Conner for Season Opener vs. Broncos
data.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs will miss left tackle Josh Simmons (back injury) and safety Chamarri Conner (knee) when they host the Denver Broncos on Monday Night Football to open the 2026 season. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson is set for his NFL debut at left tackle, a first under coach Andy Reid, while defensive tackle Chris Jones is expected to play despite a calf issue. After a 6-11 finish last year, all eyes are on how the reshuffled line holds up protecting Mahomes from stars like Nik Bonitto.

data.name: No. 1 Ohio State Faces No. 4 Texas in Austin Tonight
data.summary: ESPN's College GameDay broadcast from the University of Texas campus ahead of the 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium, with both undefeated teams coming off blowout Week 1 wins—Ohio State 56-3 over Ball State and Texas 59-7 over Texas State. Fans fired up the rivalry with playful jabs like a sign mocking Ohio State coach Ryan Day for putting ketchup on brisket, a nod to Texas barbecue pride that even GameDay called out as 'No, just no.' Texas coach Steve Sarkisian kept it simple: 'We're talking about a hell of a football game that's gonna get played tonight.' The Longhorns are slight 1.5-point home favorites, airing on ABC.

data.hook: Cam Coleman seemed to snag the deep ball over his shoulder, but it popped loose on impact—right into Jaylen McClain's waiting hands for a wild Ohio State pick.
data.name: Jaylen McClain's Fluky Interception Stuns Texas in Ohio State Clash
data.summary: In the first quarter of the top-ranked Buckeyes' primetime matchup against Texas in Austin, quarterback Arch Manning targeted wide-open receiver Cam Coleman on a deep route. Coleman hauled it in mid-air but lost control hitting the turf, allowing Ohio State safety Jaylen McClain to scoop the live ball at the Buckeyes' 19-yard line. The turnover followed Texas' earlier fumble and preserved Ohio State's 3-0 lead after a field goal, capping a rough start for the home team's offense amid a packed stadium.

data.name: Ohio State Jumps Ahead of Texas in Scorching 163-Degree Showdown
data.summary: No. 1 Ohio State grabbed an early lead over No. 4 Texas in Austin's Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium, where pre-kickoff field temperatures reached 163.6 degrees amid 97-100 degree air. Texas QB Arch Manning's deep shot to wideout Cam Coleman deflected off for a wild interception, sparking debate over whether receiver drops should count as QB stats, as former NFL QB Robert Griffin III noted. Ohio State's opportunistic defense cashed in for a 10-3 edge by the second quarter, boosted by WR Jeremiah Smith's explosive plays.

data.hook: Kayden McDonald, the Texans' hyped second-round pick, sprained his ankle in practice and now faces at least four weeks out right before the season opener.
data.name: Texans Place Rookie DT McDonald on IR, Sign Crumedy
data.summary: Houston placed rookie defensive tackle Kayden McDonald on injured reserve after he sprained his ankle during Wednesday's practice, missing the next two sessions and the opener against the Buffalo Bills. The 6-foot-3, 326-pound Ohio State product, last year's Big Ten Defensive Lineman of the Year, can return as early as Week 5. To replace him, the team signed 6-foot-4 defensive tackle Jaden Crumedy, a former sixth-round pick who played for the Panthers and Packers' practice squad, adding needed depth to the defensive line.

data.hook: Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz watched Kansas's pregame video on 'Bleeding Kansas' history and felt embarrassed for them. That fire helped his Tigers dominate 38-21.
data.name: Missouri Coach Blasts Kansas Hype Video After 38-21 Border War Win
data.summary: Kansas's 'Heroes and Villains' video highlighted Civil War-era clashes like abolitionist John Brown and slavery conflicts, framing the rivalry as deeper than sports. Drinkwitz called it 'right-versus-wrong bullcrap,' motivated his team to pull away in the second half with QB Austin Simmons' three TD passes, Jamal Roberts' 125 rushing yards and a score, plus defensive turnovers. He quipped postgame, 'We left Kansas bleeding again,' and wondered aloud if the rivalry should continue if it gets 'weird' like that—especially with unity needed after 9/11. The win marked Missouri's fifth straight in the series, played at Kansas's David Booth Stadium.

data.name: Lane Kiffin Walks with Lil Wayne and Boosie Before LSU Game
data.summary: LSU fans cheered as Kiffin led the Tiger Walk down Victory Hill with rap stars Lil Wayne and Boosie ahead of Saturday's game against Louisiana Tech. Lil Wayne rocked an LSU shirt, yellow pants, and a purple cap while joining former star Tyrann Mathieu, as the official account dubbed it 'LilWeezyana State University.' This follows last week's star guests like Livvy Dunne, building hype for the No. 8 Tigers after their 51-10 win over Clemson. Fans loved the Baton Rouge flavor, with posts calling it pure local aura.
